defaultPosture: Stop new harm first, preserve evidence, roll back the bad deploy when code/config caused the incident, and recover data from verified server/provider facts.

appHosting.safePath: Use the Firebase/App Hosting console to roll back traffic to the last known-good backend revision when a deployed app revision is the cause. This repo does not define a one-command rollback script.
appHosting.codeRollbackPath: If rollback by provider console is unavailable, create a reviewed revert commit with `git revert <bad_commit>` and let the normal GitHub/App Hosting deployment path deploy it after targeted gates pass.
preRedeployChecks: npm run check:functions if Functions changed
npm run check:firebase:rules if Firebase rules changed

firebase.safePath: Use Firebase console release history or a reviewed deploy from a known-good commit for Hosting/Functions/rules. Do not push emergency rules or Functions changes without recording the exact file, command, actor, and reason.
firebase.rulesPath: Rules are tracked in firestore.rules, database.rules.json, and storage.rules; use `npm run check:firebase:rules` before rules redeploy when possible.
firebase.manualConsoleActionRequired: Provider-console rollback may be required; no repo script can guarantee remote rollback state.

evidenceRetention: Do not delete paymentLocks, transactions, notificationDispatchLocks, notification records, queue_job_heartbeats, route runtime samples, runtime warnings, or Admin Debug evidence during first response.
Export provider receipts, affected user ids, order ids, drop ids, notification ids, idempotency keys, browser tags, refresh ids, and deployment revision ids before cleanup.

switchInventory.howToUse: If NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID_LIVE is absent after deploy, the wallet hides PayPal buttons and shows checkout unavailable. This is not a live dashboard toggle.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not stop a direct authenticated call to /api/paypal/capture for already-created PayPal orders.

switchInventory.howToUse: Admin can remove a malfunctioning Drop from the queue through the guarded queue toggle route.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not globally stop scheduled Functions or rewind already-sent notifications.

switchInventory.howToUse: The refresh route records started/completed/failed status and returns duplicate_prevented when a refresh is already running.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not disable all analytics jobs globally; use provider rollback or pause scheduled trigger externally if a job storms.

switchInventory.howToUse: Recipients with disabled browser/in-app preferences are skipped and counted by notification diagnostics.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not provide a global push-off kill switch for all notification dispatch.

switchInventory.howToUse: Bump APP_SHELL_CACHE and APP_RUNTIME_CACHE, deploy, and rely on skipWaiting/clients.claim plus network-first navigation to replace stale shells.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not let an operator change caches at runtime without a deploy.

switchInventory.howToUse: Creator messaging availability is enforced through creator settings/restrictions in chat helpers.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not provide a global chat-off kill switch.

switchInventory.howToUse: Direct client Storage reads under drops/** are denied; protected content is served through the entitlement proxy.
switchInventory.doesNotDo: Does not revoke already-leaked external media URLs by itself.

incidents.detectionSignal: Wallet checkout errors, PayPal create/capture route warnings, payment failed transactions, support reports, or live smoke purchase failure.
incidents.userImpact: Fans cannot refill GumDrops or may abandon checkout before a server-confirmed purchase completes.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Disable the visible checkout by removing/withholding the PayPal client id in the next emergency deploy or roll back to the last known-good App Hosting revision. Do not manually credit until PayPal order evidence is verified.

switchFlagAvailable.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID_LIVE readiness
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Client visibility only; not a runtime console switch and not a server capture kill switch.

incidents.manualFallback: Use Admin Users and transaction history to verify failed/completed purchase attempts. Manual balance credit is allowed only after provider proof and must use the audited admin balance route with a reason.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: Provider rollback through Firebase/App Hosting console to the previous healthy revision, or reviewed `git revert <bad_commit>` followed by normal GitHub/App Hosting deploy. No one-command rollback script exists in repo.
dataRecoverySteps: Collect orderId, PayPal capture id, userId, package, paid amount, route warning, and transaction rows.
Confirm PayPal status and custom_id user/package binding before credit.
If paid and not credited, use /api/admin/balance-backed admin UI/action to add GumDrops with support ticket reason.
If not paid or capture failed, do not credit; ask user to retry after mitigation.
Reconcile Admin Analytics commerce parity after recovery.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Checkout is temporarily unavailable while we verify payment processing. Completed payments will be reviewed from provider receipts before any balance correction.

incidents.detectionSignal: PayPal completed captures without matching paymentLocks/transactions, user balance mismatch, purchase parity warning, or support report that paid GumDrops did not appear.
incidents.userImpact: A fan may have paid but not received GumDrops.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Stop new checkout through PayPal client readiness deploy or App Hosting rollback, then reconcile already-completed orders from PayPal provider truth.

switchFlagAvailable.name: PayPal client id checkout availability
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No live wallet-crediting kill switch exists.

incidents.manualFallback: Use audited admin balance adjustment for verified paid orders. Manual DB intervention is not the first option because /api/admin/balance records an admin_adjustment transaction.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback or reviewed revert commit; run payment/unlock security validation before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Export affected paymentLocks, transactions, failed transactions, route warnings, and PayPal captures.
For each completed PayPal capture missing credit, verify user/package custom_id and expected USD amount.
Apply audited admin balance adjustment with reason referencing the support ticket and order id.
Mark duplicate or already-credited orders as no-op; never credit from client screenshots alone.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: We found a wallet credit delay. Verified completed payments will be credited from provider records.

incidents.detectionSignal: Duplicate unlock_content transactions for the same user/drop, balance double-deduction support report, unlock parity mismatch, or transaction ledger anomaly.
incidents.userImpact: A fan may lose extra GumDrops for one Drop unlock.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Roll back the bad deploy or temporarily block unlock entry points with an emergency reviewed deploy if rollback is not enough. Preserve all transactions before correction.

switchFlagAvailable.name: No global unlock kill switch identified
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Existing route is transactional and idempotent by unlockedContent, but there is no runtime off switch.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required only if duplicate ledger rows cannot be corrected through audited admin balance adjustment. Prefer admin balance adjustment for refunding excess GumDrops.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback or reviewed revert commit. Run unlock idempotency/payment validation before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Identify duplicate transactions by userId/dropId/timestamp and compare unlockedContent/unlockedContentTimestamps.
Verify the user received one entitlement only.
Refund the excess deduction with audited admin balance adjustment and support reason.
Do not delete transaction evidence; append corrective transaction metadata instead.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: We found an unlock charge issue and will return any extra GumDrops after verifying the ledger.

incidents.detectionSignal: Protected asset URL appears in public payload, unauthenticated Storage access succeeds, content proxy serves without entitlement, or user reports locked media exposure.
incidents.userImpact: Protected creator content may be visible to users without an entitlement.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Roll back the leaking deploy, redeploy deny-by-default Storage rules if rules changed, remove public payload exposure, and rotate/revoke exposed media URLs where provider controls allow.

switchFlagAvailable.name: storage.rules denies drops/** direct reads
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No live content-leak kill switch exists; leaked third-party URLs may need storage/provider cleanup.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention or Storage provider intervention is required to remove or rotate leaked content paths, replace media, or temporarily unpublish affected Drops.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: Firebase rules rollback/deploy from known-good storage.rules plus App Hosting rollback for public payload leaks. Run content media and Firebase storage rules validation before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Record affected drop ids, asset URLs, user reports, and route payload evidence.
Verify raw public routes no longer return contentUrl/contentUrls.
Disable or archive affected Drops if URLs cannot be revoked immediately.
Replace leaked assets or move them to a new protected path if needed.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Access to the affected Drop is temporarily limited while protected media is secured.

incidents.detectionSignal: Duplicate notification records, repeated browser alerts with same tag/idempotency key, FCM duplicate dispatch diagnostics, user reports, or Admin Debug duplicate counts.
incidents.userImpact: Fans may receive repeated alerts and lose trust in Drop notifications.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Stop the offending notification source: remove affected Drops from queue, roll back the deploy, or pause the scheduled trigger externally. Do not bulk resend until idempotency evidence is verified.

switchFlagAvailable.name: admin queue toggle and per-user notification preferences
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No global notification kill switch exists in tracked app code.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required to mark duplicate notification records read/cleared or to inspect notificationDispatchLocks. Preserve duplicate evidence first.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting/Functions rollback or reviewed revert. If scheduled Functions are the source, pause the scheduler in provider console until a reviewed fix deploys.
dataRecoverySteps: Collect notification ids, idempotency keys, browser tags, dispatch locks, queue activation keys, and FCM report counts.
Confirm whether duplicates are in-app records, browser displays, or FCM sends.
Remove affected Drops from queue if live/return-live loop is the source.
Mark duplicates as read/cleared only after evidence export.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Some alerts repeated. We stopped the affected send path and are cleaning duplicate notifications without changing your Drop access.

incidents.detectionSignal: Eligible users skipped unexpectedly, missing notification records, FCM missing-token/preference/permission skip counts, user reports, or Debug funnel drop-off.
incidents.userImpact: Fans may miss queued/live Drop, task, or account notifications.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Do not mass-resend immediately. Verify eligibility, preferences, tokens, idempotency locks, and dispatch outcome. Re-run only the minimal safe send path after duplicate prevention is confirmed.

switchFlagAvailable.name: No resend-all or global notification recovery switch identified
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Admin-created notifications exist, but historical per-recipient replay is not a safe one-click recovery tool.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention is required for historical replay or per-recipient repair unless a protected admin-created notification is appropriate.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: Roll back the notification deploy if code caused missing sends; pause source jobs only if retries would amplify harm.
dataRecoverySteps: Classify missing reason: permission, token, preference, dispatch failure, queue bug, or eligibility bug.
Collect recipient ids, notification ids, idempotency keys, preference state, token state, and FCM report.
If resend is needed, target only eligible affected users and use deterministic idempotency keys.
Update Admin Debug notes with skipped reason rather than fake zero counts.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Some alerts may have been delayed or missed. We are verifying eligibility before sending any replacement alert.

incidents.detectionSignal: Admin Analytics refresh duplicate_prevented warnings spike, refresh route latency/errors, materializer load, route runtime warnings, or Admin Debug refresh status stuck running.
incidents.userImpact: Admin surfaces may slow down or show delayed diagnostics, but verified snapshots should remain visible.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Stop manual refresh traffic, restrict admin refresh use, let dedupe settle, and roll back the bad deploy if refresh loops were introduced. Preserve last verified snapshots.

switchFlagAvailable.name: refresh dedupe and private no-store refresh route
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No global analytics-refresh-off switch exists in tracked app code.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required to mark a stuck refresh failed only after preserving metadata and if the UI cannot recover through route dedupe.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback or reviewed revert. If a scheduled Function causes load, pause that trigger in provider console and document the actor/time.
dataRecoverySteps: Export snapshot metadata for affected module/range cache keys.
Verify lastVerifiedAt and refreshVersion before any manual correction.
Keep last verified snapshots visible; do not delete snapshot docs.
After fix, run one forced refresh per affected module/range and record metadata.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Admin analytics refresh is delayed. Last verified data remains available while refresh is stabilized.

incidents.detectionSignal: Non-admin access to /admin or /api/admin/**, trusted-origin rejection missing on state-changing route, security alert, suspicious admin mutation, or route boundary validation failure.
incidents.userImpact: Private admin data or state-changing controls may be exposed to the wrong actor.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Roll back immediately, revoke affected admin/session credentials, tighten Firebase/Auth roles, and deploy known-good guards/rules if the boundary broke.

switchFlagAvailable.name: guardApiRequest admin and trusted-origin checks
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Guards are baseline protection; no runtime kill switch can make a broken admin route safe without deploy/rollback.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention or provider-console action may be required to remove admin claims, disable users, rotate secrets, audit affected records, or redeploy rules.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: Immediate App Hosting rollback plus Firebase rules rollback/deploy when rules changed. Run security role-boundaries validation before any redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Collect route, actor uid, auth claims, origin, request method, mutation ids, and affected records.
Revoke or rotate compromised credentials and admin claims.
Audit admin mutation logs and transaction records for unauthorized writes.
Notify affected operators/users if sensitive data was exposed.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Admin access is being locked down while we verify protected system routes. Public app access may be temporarily limited if needed.

incidents.detectionSignal: Users continue seeing old UI after deploy, offline fallback appears for valid routes, mismatched service-worker cache names, or PWA smoke failure.
incidents.userImpact: Mobile/PWA users may use stale UI or stale route assets after a deployment.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Deploy a cache-version bump and known-good service worker, or roll back to the last known-good revision. Ask affected users to close/reopen or hard refresh if needed.

switchFlagAvailable.name: APP_SHELL_CACHE/APP_RUNTIME_CACHE versioning with skipWaiting and clients.claim
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No runtime switch exists; stale clients need a new worker or user refresh.

incidents.manualFallback: No DB intervention is needed unless stale UI caused data writes. Support can guide close/reopen, browser site-data clear, or install refresh.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback for bad app shell, or deploy a service-worker cache-name bump after `npm run check:pwa-service-worker`.
dataRecoverySteps: Verify APP_SHELL_CACHE/APP_RUNTIME_CACHE names and service-worker scope.
Confirm API routes are not cached and navigation is network-first.
Bump cache names when shell/offline assets change.
Collect affected browser/device/PWA context and route.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: A mobile app refresh may be needed. Close and reopen KandyDrops, or refresh the browser tab, to load the latest version.

incidents.detectionSignal: Queued Drops fail to activate, active Drops fail to expire, auto-queued Drops loop, queue heartbeat warnings, duplicate return-live notifications, or Admin Drops schedule mismatch.
incidents.userImpact: Fans may see wrong Drop availability or receive wrong live/return-live alerts.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Remove affected Drops from queue with the admin queue toggle, pause scheduled queue processing externally if it is amplifying harm, and roll back a bad queue deploy.

switchFlagAvailable.name: admin queue toggle per Drop
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Per-Drop queue membership only; scheduled Functions must be paused in provider console if the scheduler itself is malfunctioning.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required to correct adminSettings/dropQueue, Drop validFrom/validUntil/status, or activation keys after evidence export.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting/Functions rollback or reviewed revert. Run background-job idempotency and admin CMS workflow validation before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Export queue config, affected Drop docs, queue_job_heartbeats, runtime warnings, activation keys, and notification dispatch outcomes.
Remove problematic Drops from queue or reset queue order.
Correct Drop timing/status only with explicit reason and before/after snapshot.
Re-run queue lifecycle after fix and verify no duplicate notification dispatch.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: A Drop schedule issue is being corrected. Availability may update while the queue is reconciled.

incidents.detectionSignal: Chat thread/message route errors, participant authorization failures, creator messaging unavailable reports, send latency, or route runtime samples failing.
incidents.userImpact: Fans and creators may be unable to send or read messages.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Roll back the bad deploy if chat routes changed. For a creator-specific issue, disable or adjust creator messaging settings/restrictions if existing admin tooling supports it; do not expose chat transcripts broadly.

switchFlagAvailable.name: creator messaging availability settings
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: No global chat outage kill switch is implemented.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required to repair a specific thread, participant id, read marker, or creator setting. Keep participant boundaries intact.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback or reviewed revert. Run chat route tests and security role-boundary validation before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Collect threadId, sender uid, creator/user participant ids, route error, and transaction/accrual evidence if a paid message failed.
Verify participant authorization before exposing any record.
Refund paid message cost through audited balance adjustment only if spend occurred without message delivery.
Repair thread metadata only with before/after evidence.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Creator messaging is temporarily delayed. Any paid message issue will be checked against the chat and wallet ledger.

incidents.detectionSignal: Creator profile route not-found spike, support reports, username lookup failures, public Drops missing for active creators, or creator routing telemetry anomaly.
incidents.userImpact: Fans may be unable to open creator profiles or public creator Drops.
incidents.immediateMitigation: Roll back route/profile changes, repair username/status/role data for affected creators, and verify public payload sanitization remains intact.

switchFlagAvailable.name: No creator-profile rollback switch identified
switchFlagAvailable.limitations: Creator 404 repair is data/deploy recovery, not a flag.

incidents.manualFallback: Manual DB intervention may be required to repair username, role, status, creatorSettings, or public Drop metadata. Do not expose private creator data during repair.
incidents.rollbackCommandPath: App Hosting rollback or reviewed revert. Run creator profile/content media/security validations before redeploy.
dataRecoverySteps: Collect usernames, creator uids, role/status fields, creatorSettings, and public Drop ids.
Verify creator is public and active before changing routing data.
Repair username index/profile fields or route regression.
Confirm public route returns sanitized Drops only.
incidents.userCommunicationNote: Some creator profiles may be temporarily unavailable while routing is corrected.
